title: Using AI assistance on Space Wars 3: keeping browser UI changes consistent with a shared design system
author: Alive-Scientist-8289
selftext:
I’m developing Space Wars 3, a free three-player browser MOBA, with AI assistance. One concrete part of the workflow is keeping generated UI changes inside the same design system instead of letting every feature invent its own styling.

The project has shared HUD tokens and components, plus a visual reference. The repository instructions tell the coding agent to reuse those tokens, preserve safe areas and responsive geometry, and check the real HUD on desktop and mobile. The browser source is classic scripts sharing a global scope, so script order is another constraint that has to remain explicit.

There are two different checks here: offline tests can catch syntax, script-order and snapshot-contract problems; browser checks have to examine whether the tutorial, controls and HUD actually work together. A passing code check alone is not evidence that the interface feels good to a new player.

That is the part of AI-assisted development I’m trying to keep disciplined as features accumulate: give the agent concrete shared references and verify the integrated result. I’m not claiming the game is bug-free or that everything was generated in one prompt. AI also assisted writing this post.

The current game is playable here: [https://www.spacewars3.online/play/index.html](https://www.spacewars3.online/play/index.html)

Guest entry and solo practice are available. I’d be interested in how others prevent visual inconsistency as AI-assisted game projects grow.

comments.author: seahorse-emoji
comments.body:
I've found that in for UI in addition to a design system creating an informal communication language with an agent about screenspace and where specific elements should live is really helpful.

I was working on mobile so we started talking of the screen as a 6 x 12 grid. So I could say things like the element should be generally in A0 to B2 space etc.

So much easier than top left and middle ish right. 

You can also fold this into a skill
